passage:
The elevator in Grandma's apartment building broke on Sunday. She lived on the fourth floor, so going outside became difficult.
Her neighbors made a plan. One brought groceries. Another took out her trash. A teenager helped carry her laundry downstairs.
The repair took three days. When the elevator worked again, Grandma baked cookies and gave them to everyone who helped.
A neighbor said, "You do not need to thank us so much."
Grandma answered, "I am not only thanking you for carrying things. I am thanking you for remembering me."
The broken elevator was inconvenient, but it showed something good. People living in the same building were not just people behind doors. They could become a small community.
